messages:
ana_cs: Hey team — customer hitting a burst of 401s across multiple endpoints starting ~2028-02-11 14:22 UTC. They provided one request id: req_0a1b2c3d. Can someone pull server-side logs and confirm whether this is an auth failure or upstream token issue?

jules_engineer: Thanks, Ana. Can you paste the full response headers (if available) and exact timestamp for that request? 401s could be edge vs control-plane.

ana_cs: Here's what the customer captured quickly:
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Date: Sun, 11 Feb 2028 14:22:31 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: req_0a1b2c3d

{"error":"Invalid API key"}
```
They say it started right after a billing update. :thinking:

matt_infra: OK. I can run a backend log search. Quick note on retention: hosted request logs are hot for 30 days, then move to archived storage for up to 365 days — archive restores take a few hours. If this is >30d we may need an archive restore.

matt_infra: Running a live query now. Use this Lucene-style search in the log UI: `json.request_id: \"req_0a1b2c3d\" OR http.headers.X-Request-ID: \"req_0a1b2c3d\"` — widen to `req_0a1b*` if you only have prefix. Also try `span.id`/`trace.id` fields if traces were sampled.

ana_cs: The customer also asked for a curl they can run to repro for support. I sent this but they say it still returns 401: `curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_redacted' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`

jules_engineer: For repro + better debug, have them include the request id header on the client side when they call. Example curl that echoes headers and returns body so we capture everything: 
```
curl -i -s -D - -o /tmp/body.json \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  -H \"X-Request-ID: req_0a1b2c3d\" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
cat /tmp/body.json
```
Tell them to paste the full output. That helps match logs exactly.

oncall_sre: FYI if we need to dig in the serving tier, include the route and model name. Auth failures sometimes happen if requests were routed to a fallback infra (old key config).

matt_infra: Query result so far: found 3 events matching req_0a1b2c3d in us-east-1 control plane around 2028-02-11 14:22:31. Raw entry shows `auth: token_lookup_failed -> 401`. Pushing the snippet to this thread.

matt_infra: Snippet (redacted):
```
@2028-02-11T14:22:31Z service=auth node=auth-3 msg=\"token lookup failed\" request_id=req_0a1b2c3d user_id=null reason=\"billing: account_suspended\"
```

jules_engineer: That lines up with the customer's billing note. Looks like the key was flagged as suspended by our billing backend. We should confirm whether there's a billing webhook failure.

ana_cs: Customer says they have an active invoice payment pending — they expected a grace flow. Can we confirm whether a grace-window change was rolled out last week?

matt_infra: I see a config change on 2028-02-04 toggling `billing.enforce_immediate_suspend=true` in prod. Rolling back would be a product decision. For now, I can confirm behavior: suspended accounts return 401 at auth tier.

jules_engineer: Action items: (1) Ana — collect full curl output + route/model from customer, (2) Ana — ask billing to confirm the webhook and invoice state, (3) Matt — if customer requests, open an archive restore for any older events.

ana_cs: On it. Sending repro curl with `-D -` now and asking billing. Will attach output when I have it. :thumbsup:

log-archiver-bot: Archive restore ticket created: ARCH-4521. ETA ~6 hours for restore of 2028-02-04..2028-02-11 window. Requestor: matt_infra.

matt_infra: If anyone needs the exact log query to paste into the UI: `service:auth AND msg:\"token lookup failed\" AND request_id: \"req_0a1b2c3d\"` — that should pull the auth flow. If you only have a prefix, use wildcard at the end.

jules_engineer: Also sending a quick helper to the customer to capture a debug bundle (curl + env):
```
# capture headers + body
TOKEN=sk_live_redacted
curl -i -s -D debug_headers.txt -o debug_body.json \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  -H \"X-Request-ID: req_0a1b2c3d\" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# compress and upload to support
tar czf debug_bundle_req_0a1b2c3d.tgz debug_headers.txt debug_body.json
```

ana_cs: Thanks all — I'll update the customer and post the debug bundle when they send it. Closing loop once billing confirms.

matt_infra: Good plan. If billing wants a temporary lift we can do a one-time override but must log it.

ana_cs: Noted.
